this movie emphasizes life's hardships and how hard it is to keep yourself together when all these things keep going wrong. I love the different scenes when it was just the dad and his son when they were goofing off. That one scene when the dad and his son we're trying to figure out where to go and the dad changed the son's view to  pretending like they went through a time machine and can all of a sudden see dinosaurs reminded me that the way we look at life in the middle of whatever we're going through impacts what we go through so much. Although everything was just going wrong, the dad didn't want his son to be upset and he just completely made what seemed to be a hard place to something that was more of that joy we all desire. looking for the light peeking through when it feels like everything else is just darkness might really just be the answer to the pursuit to happiness but true happiness comes from God so when they did go to church and they were singing that one song about "God, please don't take away the mountains just help me get through them" shows that we need the struggles and we need the hardships because that's what builds us and without them we wouldn't have any growth. “maybe happiness is something that we can only pursue and maybe we can actually never have it.” Will and Jaden Smith took this movie to the next level. Will Smith’s delivery of Chris’s emotions and frustrations is very well done. I’m shocked I haven’t heard more about Pursuit of Happiness, and particularly its talented cast. I noticed a good bit of messaging in some of the cinematography I originally overlooked. Although this movie is meant to be inspirational, I more so interpreted its darker undertones. Some of the most grueling, inhumane corners of capitalism are highlighted well in Pursuit of Happiness, even so in the name of the movie. Jaden Smith’s character, Christopher, adds so much to this movie; his relationship and perception of his dad in particular stood out to me. His loyalty even through hardships that no one should endure. Him bottling in the feeling of his mom leaving because of him. I certainly recommend Pursuit of Happiness.

Hayat, o duvardaki yazı gibi hatalarla, yamalarla ve eksiklerle doludur. Orijinal kelimedeki(happiness) "i" harfi yerine "y" harfinin gelmesi, mutluluğun başkalarının sana verdiği bir şey değil, senin kendi ellerinle şekillendirdiğin, sana özel (Y) bir şey olduğunu simgeler. Ve bu filmden iki sonuç çıkardım: 1.Mutluluk Garanti Edilmez, "Aranır" Evren, bize mutluluk borçlu değil. Mutluluk gökten inen bir hediye değil; sokaklarda koşarak, yeri geldiğinde kan ter içinde kalarak ve tırnaklarınla kazıyarak "kovalaman" (pursuit) gereken bir hedeftir. 2.Mazeret Üretmemek Hedefimiz ne olursa olsun karşımıza engeller hep çıkacak ve asla engellerden dolayı pes etmemeliyiz. Engellerdir aslında bizi güçlendiren. Sadece önüne bakıp içinde bulunduğun durumdan kurtulmaya bak. Ve bu replik:Birinin sana bir şey yapamayacağını söylemesine asla izin verme. Benim bile. Bir hayalin varsa onu korumalısın. İnsanlar kendi yapamadıkları şeyleri senin de yapamayacağını söylerler. Bir şey istiyorsan, git ve al. O kadar." En sevdiğim film oldu ve öyle kalacak...

complete perspective-changing movie. got me tearing up and stuff yo! but genuinely this movie was amazingly captivating from beginning to end. the acting was phenomenal, will smith does an amazing job portraying gardner throughout the film and doing his story justice. his story is truly outstanding and motivating. this is honestly some of the best cinematography i’ve ever seen in a movie also, there were scenes and shots that were executed perfectly throughout the entire film, from the cityscape at the end to the bathroom scene. the way that they split up the entire story into different sections was perfect too. i think portraying his ability to grow as a person and through his own struggles of not being able to provide for his family through the many different phases of his life was really effective in getting the theme across and made it very heartfelt. lowkey don’t even understand how they made this masterpiece so motivational and inspiring and just made it in general. the soundtrack was also incredible and the needle drops are perfectly executed. the movie really just shows the importance of perseverance and conveys humanity really effectively to me. i love the idea happ(y)ness is a constant pursuit that we have to work for daily. really speaks to how much one moment can truly define you. ridiculously good.

esse filme me deixa com uma sensação muito estranha, pq ao mesmo tempo que ele me da esperança ele tbm me deixa completamente destruida. ver o chris passando por tudo aquilo enquanto tenta cuidar do filho e ainda continuar acreditando que as coisas podem melhorar eh muito doloroso o que mais gosto eh que ele não desiste mesmo quando parece que não tem mais nada dando certo. ele perde dinheiro, perde a casa, passa por situações humilhantes e mesmo assim continua tentando, principalmente por causa do filho. e eu acho muito bonito como a relação dos dois eh o que faz ele continuar, pq ele não ta lutando só por ele, ele quer conseguir dar uma vida melhor pro filho e o filme mostra muito bem que as coisas não acontecem do nada. ele não simplesmente acorda um dia e tudo fica perfeito, ele passa por um monte de merda antes de conseguir alguma coisa. tem momentos que da vontade de entrar no filme e falar pra ele parar um pouco, descansar, pq parece que nada vai dar certo acho muito forte tbm aquela ideia de não deixar os outros dizerem o que vc consegue ou não fazer. principalmente quando ele fala pro filho que, se ele quer alguma coisa, precisa proteger aquele sonho. não pq vai ser facil, mas justamente pq provavelmente vai ter gente tentando fazer ele desistir e o que mais me pega eh que no final a felicidade não parece ser sobre ficar rico ou ter sucesso. eh sobre finalmente poder respirar depois de passar tanto tempo sobrevivendo. depois de tudo que ele passou, aquele momento simples de perceber que conseguiu me destruiu não acho que seja um filme perfeito e algumas partes são bem feitas pra arrancar lagrima mesmo, mas sinceramente não importa. eu terminei com aquela sensação de querer reclamar da vida por reclamar de coisas pequenas e ao mesmo tempo abraçar meu filho se eu tivesse um um filme sobre continuar tentando quando vc ja não sabe mais de onde tirar forças. e talvez seja isso que faça ele doer tanto
